lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé has no summary or target-role framing.
items.because: Readers have to infer that you are pursuing product management.

items.says: The product and operations experience does not read as one coherent story.
items.because: The career direction is not immediately clear.

items.says: Only one clearly titled product-management position is shown, and it was an internship.
items.because: No explicit post-MBA PM role appears on the résumé.

items.says: Product strategy, go-to-market, and product-lifecycle evidence is not listed.
items.because: Some PM postings may require it.

items.says: Consider whether both education locations add value.
items.because: They use space without helping establish PM fit.

items.says: The current Diesel Mechanic role makes the post-MBA career direction hard to read.
items.because: It follows an MBA and product internship without explaining the direction.

items.says: Explain the rebuild work's relevance through operational constraints, coordination, or reliability outcomes.
items.because: Otherwise it may look like a sharp departure from product experience.

items.says: The maintenance and recordkeeping bullet needs a meaningful outcome or a reassessment of its space.
items.because: It reads as routine work for a PM application.

items.says: Show the scorecards' scale, a decision they informed, or an improvement they produced.
items.because: The bullet establishes responsibility but not what changed because of the work.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period for the pick-error reduction.
Add the business consequence of fewer pick errors, if known.
Define what the forecast-error measure represents.
Say whether the reduction held over 12 quarters or was the final observed result.
Separate the main achievement from secondary responsibilities or shorten the activity list.
items.because: The many activities make the measured impact harder to absorb.

items.says: Clarify how the 1,800 driver hours saved were estimated.
Clarify how time to first payment was calculated.
Say whether the result covers the whole pilot cohort or only a subset.
Describe the move from 61% to 66% as five percentage points, not five percent.
items.because: Percentage change and percentage-point change are different.

items.says: Clarify what shipping the flow to all merchants covers.
Say whether the measured lift was sustained after rollout.
The checkout conversion result is repeated in another bullet.
items.because: The overlap makes the résumé look less substantial than the work may be.

items.says: Clarify how Reach was scored in the RICE method.
items.because: Tickets a feature would close may describe support-ticket reduction rather than conventional Reach.

items.says: Make the roadmap decision influenced by the discovery and business-case work clearer.
items.because: The sequence of activities obscures that decision.

items.says: Distinguish your recommendation from the final decision-maker's authority.
items.because: Your role in setting the priority is unclear.

items.says: The checkout A/B-test bullet overlaps substantially with the earlier conversion bullet.
items.because: It repeats the conversion result without a clearly distinct contribution.

items.says: Explain precisely what was randomized and what the reported outcome measures.
items.because: Session-level assignment and customer conversion are related but not the same unit.

items.says: Distinguish funding approval from an actual rollout to the additional regions.
items.because: A reader could confuse approval with deployment.

items.says: Define whether 3,100 students were reached, registered, or eligible to use the app.
Make sure the 9-tonne figure reflects measured redistribution.
Support the claim that the redistributed food would otherwise have been wasted.
The stated 150% weekly-active-user increase conflicts with the counts.
items.because: An increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%.

items.says: Clarify the period over which weekly active users increased.
Say whether both counts use the same weekly-active-user definition.
The fill-rate change is called a 20% increase rather than a 20-percentage-point increase.
items.because: The stated rates go from 75% to 95%.

items.says: Clarify the fill-rate measurement period.
Say whether the fill-rate change was observed consistently across both halls.
Distinguish the modeled annual saving from realized savings.
items.because: Pilot funding does not show that the full projected saving was achieved.

items.says: The pilot-approval outcome is repeated in another practicum bullet.
items.because: Both bullets appear to describe the same approval.

items.says: Use an active construction and clarify your role in the intake work.
items.because: The passive wording hides what you did.

items.says: Specify the change adopted and its effect, if measured.
items.because: The bullet describes activity without showing its impact.

items.says: The pilot approval appears to repeat the outcome in the first practicum bullet.
items.because: It spends space on the same approval rather than a separate contribution.

items.says: Show more depth or scope in the product skills.
items.because: The list names methods without indicating the strength of those capabilities.

items.says: Indicate what you used each listed tool for.
items.because: The tools list is short and gives little detail.

items.says: SQL or analytics depth is not evidenced.
items.because: Some PM postings may require it, though tools should not be added unless actually used.
